note: Independent cohorts confirm behavioral problems/dysregulation occur in approximately 62% to 85% of affected individuals rather than being an obligatory diagnostic feature.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 21 individuals with heterozygous pathogenic FBXO11 variants, behavioural dysregulation was present in 62% of patients.

source.title: Defining FBXO11-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical, Molecular and Facial Assessment of 21 Patients
source.quote: Mild intellectual disability (86%), facial dysmorphism (67%), hypotonia (62%), and behavioural dysregulation (62%) were the most prevalent features.

evidence.text: In an earlier cohort of 20 individuals with de novo FBXO11 variants, behavioral problems were documented in 17 of 20 (85%) individuals.

source.title: De novo variants in the F-box protein FBXO11 in 20 individuals with a variable neurodevelopmental disorder
source.quote: They present with mild to severe developmental delay associated with a range of features including short (4/20) or tall (2/20) stature, obesity (5/20), microcephaly (4/19) or macrocephaly (2/19), behavioral problems (17/20), seizures (5/20), cleft lip or palate or bifid uvula (3/20), and minor skeletal anomalies.
